Key takeaways

  • GMV grew from €0.73M in 2021 to €2.04M in 2025, and orders from 36k to 74k.
  • Each order lost €1.03 in 2021. In 2025 it made €1.83, mainly because Forkly-funded discounts fell from 6.9% to 0.7% of GMV.
  • Contribution margin is 6.4%, down 1.3 pp on 2024, as Plus members (42% of orders) pay almost no delivery fee.
  • The delivery rating recovered from 3.74 in 2022 to 4.51.
Customers →

Key takeaways

  • Year-over-year retention fell from 90% to 71% after the 2022 service problems and has stayed near 68% since.
  • Returning customers placed 71% of 2025 orders.
  • Champions are 30% of customers but bring in 69% of GMV over the last 12 months.
  • Plus members order 3.9 times a year, against 1.8 for non-members, with about the same basket.
← OverviewRestaurants →

Key takeaways

  • Warsaw is the largest city with 23% of 2025 GMV, followed by Krakow and Helsinki.
  • Grocery, launched in 2024, is already the largest category at 17% of GMV.
  • The top 20% of partners make 40% of GMV, so restaurant revenue is far less concentrated than customer revenue.
← CustomersOperations →

Key takeaways

  • The late rate peaked at 32% in 2022 and was 5.1% in 2025. Average delivery time is 30.7 minutes.
  • Ratings stay at 4.3 or higher until an order is 5 minutes late, then fall to 3.5 at 5-10 minutes and 2.5 at 20+ minutes.
  • Heavy rain raises the late rate from 11.8% to 18.8%.
  • Support tickets are down to 2.4 per 100 orders, with a median resolution time of 1.0 h.
← RestaurantsMarketing →

Key takeaways

  • Take rate is 32.3% and net revenue €659k in 2025.
  • Marketing spend fell from €566k in 2022 to €162k, and CAC from €43.56 to €26.98.
  • Referral Rewards is the cheapest channel at €26 per signup; Search costs €49.
  • Since 2022, customers whose first order used a promo are 7-10 pp more likely to order again within 90 days.
